subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox container exits immediately when no-new-privileges is applied (exec /usr/bin/sleep: operation not permitted)

question: Should OpenClaw allow Docker sandbox startup recovery by exposing an explicit dangerous `no-new-privileges` opt-out, by using diagnostic-only guidance, or by silently falling back after EPERM?
rationale: The code fix is straightforward, but the policy choice changes sandbox hardening and cannot be safely chosen by cleanup automation.

options.title: Explicit dangerous opt-out with diagnostics
options.body: Add a named opt-out that defaults to secure behavior, reports as dangerous in security/doctor output, and requires real Docker proof for both default and opt-out modes.

options.title: Diagnostic-only recovery
options.body: Keep the hardening flag unconditional and improve status/session/doctor messages so affected operators can identify the host-level Docker incompatibility without weakening OpenClaw defaults.

options.title: Automatic fallback after EPERM
options.body: Retry without the hardening flag on the specific startup failure, accepting that users may run with a weaker sandbox unless the fallback is made highly visible.

recommendation.title: Explicit dangerous opt-out with diagnostics
recommendation.body: Add a named opt-out that defaults to secure behavior, reports as dangerous in security/doctor output, and requires real Docker proof for both default and opt-out modes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent commits show ownership of sandbox Docker create-args and dangerous override handling, which are the central decision surfaces here.
